_readme: This one file sets what the workbook asks. Change a title, a question or the order here and both the page and the server follow. Each section needs a unique id (letters only). 'toolkit' tells the search where to look: 'search' is extra words to look for, 'sections' are toolkit sections to favour (matched on the start of their name), and 'always' is a chapter that is always included. After editing, run ./deploy.sh so the server picks it up.

project.label: The building
project.hint: What kind of housing, how many homes, and who lives there.

project.label: The space you have in mind
project.hint: A storage room, a community room corner, a closet off the lobby. Rough size if you know it.

project.label: Who is working on this
project.hint: Staff, resident leaders, partners. Names or roles.

project.label: Rough budget
project.hint: What you have or expect for opening and the first year. A range is fine.

project.label: What residents have told you so far
project.hint: Anything they have asked for or worried about. Leave blank if you have not asked yet.

sections.title: Purpose and people
sections.brief: Why this library of things, who it is for, and who will carry it.
questions: Why does this building need a library of things? What would be different for residents a year from now?
Who is it for? Residents only, or neighbors too?
Who will carry it day to day, and who else needs to be in the circle so it does not rest on one person?

toolkit.search: why who vision motivation team shared responsibility community challenges guiding questions

sections.title: Resident needs and engagement
sections.brief: How residents shape what the library holds and how it runs.
questions: How have you asked residents what they would borrow, or how will you?
Who is hard to reach in the building (language, schedule, trust), and what would help?
How will residents keep having a say once it is open?

toolkit.search: needs assessment engagement survey community input listening residents outreach

sections.title: Space and setup
sections.brief: Where it lives in the building, how it is laid out, and how people get to it.
questions: Describe the space: where it is, how big, who holds the key today.
When could it be open, and who would be there?
What needs to change before opening (shelving, power, locks, signs, access for people with mobility needs)?

toolkit.search: space design layout storage shelving access hours apartment building room accessibility

sections.title: Items: what to stock and how to get them
sections.brief: The opening inventory, where items come from, and how they stay in working order.
questions: What are the first 15 to 30 items you expect residents to want?
Where will items come from: purchase, donations, partners?
Who checks, cleans and repairs items when they come back?

toolkit.search: sourcing items inventory donations purchasing popular items maintenance repair cleaning

sections.title: Policies and lending system
sections.brief: How borrowing works, and what tracks it.
questions: Who can borrow, for how long, and does it cost anything?
What should happen when something comes back late, broken, or not at all?
How will you track loans: lending software, a spreadsheet, a paper ledger? Any constraint from your property management systems?

toolkit.search: policies lending system loan period late fees damaged items waiver software inventory management checkout

sections.title: Staffing, volunteers and resident roles
sections.brief: Who opens the door, who looks after items, and how residents take on roles.
questions: How many staff hours per week can you commit, and whose?
What roles could residents or volunteers hold, and is there a stipend or other thank you?
How will people be trained and supported?

toolkit.search: volunteers staffing roles shifts training membership recruiting coordinator hiring

sections.title: Budget and funding
sections.brief: What it costs to open and to run for a year, and where the money comes from.
questions: What do you expect to spend before opening, and on what?
What will it cost to run each year, and which line in your budget does that sit on?
Which funding sources are realistic: operating budget, resident services funds, grants, sponsors, fees?

toolkit.search: budget operational costs income fundraising grants earned revenue startup costs membership fees

sections.title: Insurance, risk and governance
sections.brief: How risk is handled, what cover is needed, and who decides.
questions: What have your insurer, risk manager or lawyer said so far, if anything?
Which items or situations worry you most?
Who makes decisions about the library, and how are residents part of that?

toolkit.search: insurance liability waiver risk governance decision making board community governance safety

sections.title: Partners
sections.brief: Who to work with nearby, and what each side brings.
questions: Who do you already work with that could help (tool libraries, the public library, nonprofits, city agencies, local businesses)?
What do you most need from a partner: items, expertise, volunteers, money, repair skills?
What can you offer in return?

toolkit.search: partnerships selecting partners nonprofit government business public library tool library ecosystem

sections.title: Outreach and launch event
sections.brief: How residents hear about it, and what opening day looks like.
questions: How do residents hear about things in the building today, and what works?
What would a good opening day look like?
Does it have a name yet? Any workshops or repair events you want to run in the first months?

toolkit.search: communications marketing brand outreach launch event workshops repair events flyers social media

sections.title: Timeline to opening day
sections.brief: The steps between now and opening, in order, with who does each.
questions: What is already done, and what must happen before anything else can?
What fixed dates or approvals are you working around?
Who owns the timeline?

toolkit.search: timeline planning steps phases getting started launch opening first year milestones now what
